title: Quentin and the Letters
premise: Cyrus Ishikawa, a ghostwriter who has spent a decade erasing himself from other people's stories, is hired through an anonymous literary agency to correspond with a dying stranger who wants one honest letter a week. The stranger turns out to be Margot Vane, the rival memoirist whose book Cyrus is secretly writing and whose testimony, ten years ago, destroyed his brother's appeal. As the letters deepen into love, Cyrus must choose between the confession that could free his brother's memory and the woman who is finally teaching him that survival is not the same as living. He tells her the truth in the final letter, and she answers with the sentence she rehearsed for a decade too: she already knew, and forgave him first.
about_author: Sebastian Crane is the pen name of a former court stenographer who spent fifteen years transcribing other people's confessions before writing any of his own. He lives in a coastal town where he teaches letter-writing workshops and refuses to own a telephone.

chapters.title: The Agency of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Cyrus accepts a lucrative but strange assignment: weekly anonymous letters to a terminally ill stranger, mediated by a discreet agency. In his cramped apartment, surrounded by the ghostwritten memoir of Margot Vane, he writes his first letter as 'Q.' POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: cautious detachment masking old grief.

chapters.title: Margot's Last Honest Year
chapters.summary: Margot Vane, dying and furious at the sanitized memoir her publisher wants, signs up for the pen-pal program hoping for one relationship without an audience. She receives Q's guarded first letter and writes back with disarming bluntness. POV: Margot. Emotional beat: defiant hope in the face of a countdown.

chapters.title: Rules of Correspondence
chapters.summary: The agency's rules forbid real names, addresses, and photographs. Cyrus, ghostwriting Margot's chapters by day, finds her voice on the page eerily familiar and dismisses the coincidence. His brother Daniel's appeal file sits unopened in a drawer. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: the first crack in his practiced invisibility.

chapters.title: What the Tide Takes
chapters.summary: Margot describes the coastal house where she grew up, and Cyrus realizes with cold dread that his anonymous correspondent is the same Margot Vane who testified against Daniel ten years ago. He nearly quits, then keeps writing, telling himself he'll gather her confession instead. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: guilt disguised as purpose.

chapters.title: Letters We Never Sent
chapters.summary: Margot confesses she has spent ten years writing unsent letters of apology to a man she wronged, though she never names him. Cyrus recognizes himself in her guilt and answers more honestly than he intended. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: two liars telling accidental truths.

chapters.title: The Memoir Machine
chapters.summary: Cyrus interviews Margot in person for the ghostwritten memoir, their first meeting. She is sharp, funny, and nothing like the villain of his family's story, which infuriates him. He hides his face behind professional neutrality. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: hatred losing its grip, resented.

chapters.title: Q, Unmasked to One
chapters.summary: Margot begins to suspect Q's identity through a repeated phrase that echoes the trial transcript she has reread for a decade. She says nothing, testing him with a question only Daniel's brother could answer. POV: Margot. Emotional beat: terror and tenderness entangled.

chapters.title: The Sentence Rehearsed
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: the trial, Daniel's conviction, and the moment young Cyrus decided that truth was a luxury for people who could afford it. The chapter reveals what Margot actually witnessed and why her testimony was coerced. POV: Margot. Emotional beat: the weight of a decade of silence.

chapters.title: Deadline in the Margins
chapters.summary: The memoir's publisher moves up the deadline; Margot's doctors move up her prognosis. Cyrus is now writing her life story while hiding his own from her, and the two projects begin to bleed together on the page. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: the cost of surviving by splitting yourself in two.

chapters.title: A Room with No Witnesses
chapters.summary: Working late at Margot's house, Cyrus finds her box of unsent letters and reads one addressed to 'the brother of the boy I buried in words.' He flees before she returns, and she knows he read it. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: exposure without confession.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Daniel, out on compassionate release and dying slower than Margot, urges Cyrus to take the agency's money and let the past stay buried. Cyrus's loyalty to his brother collides with the truth he owes Margot and himself. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: love as a debt with compounding interest.

chapters.title: The Confession Draft
chapters.summary: Cyrus writes the letter that says everything—his name, Daniel's name, the decade of rehearsed sentences—and cannot mail it. Margot, meanwhile, tells her editor the memoir will be published under Cyrus Ishikawa's name, not hers. POV: Margot. Emotional beat: generosity as a weapon of love.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: The agency's broker, fearing scandal, reveals to Margot's publisher that Q is the ghostwriter and that the memoir is a fraud of attribution. Margot learns Cyrus's name from an enemy before she could learn it from a friend. POV: Margot. Emotional beat: betrayal arriving secondhand.

chapters.title: The Week of Silence
chapters.summary: No letters come. Cyrus, believing Margot has cut him off, finishes the memoir's final chapter and slips his own confession into the acknowledgments. Margot, hospitalized, writes a letter she instructs the agency to deliver only after she's gone. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: the terrible politeness of people protecting each other from the truth.

chapters.title: Daniel's Testimony
chapters.summary: Daniel, having read Cyrus's draft confession over his shoulder, finally tells his own truth: Margot's testimony was coerced by the prosecutor who threatened her, and Daniel knew for ten years and said nothing to spare Cyrus. POV: Daniel. Emotional beat: loyalty revealed as its own kind of lie.

chapters.title: The Hospital Letter
chapters.summary: Cyrus breaks every rule and goes to Margot in person, letter in hand. She is furious, then wrecked, then honest: she has known who Q was since chapter eight's phrase, and she kept writing because the letters were the only place she was brave. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: the rehearsed sentence finally spoken, and it changes nothing and everything.

chapters.title: What Survives a Trial
chapters.summary: Together they reconstruct the coercion: a retired clerk's notes, Margot's original statement, the prosecutor's pressure. Cyrus must decide whether to reopen Daniel's case knowing it will burn the memoir, the agency, and his career. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: choosing justice over safety for the first time.

chapters.title: Publication Day
chapters.summary: The memoir publishes with Cyrus's name on the cover, his confession in the acknowledgments, and Margot's coerced testimony exposed in its final chapter. The industry erupts; the prosecutor's office stonewalls; Daniel reads it in his hospice bed and weeps. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: ruin and release arriving together.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Margot, against her doctors' advice, testifies at the reopened hearing and names the man who threatened her, on the record, in public, with Cyrus holding her hand outside the door. POV: Margot. Emotional beat: the price of survival finally paid in full.

chapters.title: Exoneration
chapters.summary: Daniel's conviction is vacated; he lives long enough to hear the verdict and to tell Margot he forgave her years ago, that the only person who needed forgiving was himself. He dies eleven days later, at peace. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: grief with no guilt underneath it for the first time.

chapters.title: The Last Letter
chapters.summary: Margot, fading, dictates her final letter to Q—not the one the agency held, but a new one: an apology for the decade, a thank-you for the year, and a request that he write her story honestly now that she can read it. Cyrus reads it aloud at her bedside. POV: Margot. Emotional beat: love stated plainly, without time to hide behind.

chapters.title: Quentin and the Letters
chapters.summary: A year later, Cyrus publishes the true story under his own name and the title she chose for it, her middle name revealed at last: Quentin was her father's name, and she gave it to her stranger because he was the only honest man she knew. He writes the final letter to her, and mails it to the tide. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into a life no longer invisible.
